paper.title: Censored Semi-Bandits: A Framework for Resource Allocation with Censored Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Censored Semi-Bandits with identical threshold for all arms (CSB-ST)
unmapped: Learner allocates a divisible resource Q across K arms; an arm's Bernoulli loss is incurred and observed only if its allocation is below an unknown common threshold theta_c (censored feedback)
The common threshold theta_c is unknown and must be estimated; once known the problem is equivalent to multiple-play MAB with m = K - M arms played
The learner knows the resource budget Q and a lower bound epsilon on all mean losses
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we focus on the particular case of the censored semi bandits problem where $\theta_i=\theta_c$ for all $i \in [K]$. With abuse of notation, we continue to denote an instance of CSB with the same threshold as $(\bmu, \theta_c, Q)$, where $\theta_c \in (0,1]$ is the same threshold.

unmapped: Learner allocates a divisible resource Q; arm i's Bernoulli loss is incurred and observed only if allocation a_i < theta_i with arm-dependent unknown thresholds theta_i; feasible superarms are determined by a 0-1 knapsack problem
The learner knows Q, a lower bound epsilon on mean losses, and the slack gamma = r/K (residual resource per arm)
settings.definition_quote: we consider a more difficult problem where the threshold may not be the same for all arms. ... The CSB problem with known threshold vector theta is regret equivalent to a combinatorial semi-bandits where Oracle uses KP(mu,theta,Q) to identify the optimal subset of arms.

symbols.n_Theta: |Theta| = size of candidate threshold set {Q/K, ..., min(1,Q)}
symbols.nabla_m: maximum per-round regret over feasible allocations
symbols.mu_KM: mean loss mu_{K-M} of the (K-M)-th smallest-loss arm
symbols.sum_bottomM: sum over arms i in [K]\[K-M] (the M highest-loss arms)
symbols.eps_mu: lower bound epsilon on all mean losses

conditions: mu_1 >= epsilon > 0 (all mean losses at least epsilon)
mu_{K-M} < mu_{K-M+1} (unique set of bottom-M arms)

source.label: thm:regretSameThreshold
source.quote: Let $\mu_1\geq \epsilon>0$, $W_T = {\log(T\log_2(|\Theta|))}/{\max\{1, \floor{Q}\}\log(1/(1-\epsilon))}$, $\mu_{K-M} < \mu_{K-M+1},$ and $T>W_T\log_2(|\Theta|)$. Set $\delta=1/T$ in CSB-ST. Then the regret of CSB-ST is upper bound as \EE{\Regret_T} \le W_T\log_2{(|\Theta|)}\nabla_m + O((\log T)^{2/3}) + \sum_{i \in [K]\setminus [K-M]} \frac{(\mu_i-\mu_{K-M} )\log {T}}{d( \mu_{K-M},\mu_i)}.

results.notes: Only the (log T)^{2/3} term is in O(); the other terms are explicit. Regret defined through means (pseudo-regret). Corollary 1 states asymptotic optimality, by comparison with the Anantharam et al. lower bound. Intermediate Theorems 1 and 2 (appendix) are not recorded separately.

symbols.gamma: residual resource after optimal allocation divided by K
symbols.nabla_m: maximum per-round regret over feasible allocations
symbols.Z_eta: sum_i max_{S_a: i in S_a} |S_a|/(nabla_a - 2(k_star^2+2) eta)
symbols.k_star: number of arms receiving insufficient resource in the optimal allocation
symbols.eta: free analysis parameter with nabla_a > 2(k_star^2+2) eta for all a
symbols.eps_mu: lower bound epsilon on all mean losses

conditions: mu_1 >= epsilon (all mean losses at least epsilon)
eta such that for all feasible a, nabla_a > 2(k_star^2+2) eta

source.label: thm:regretDiffThreshold
source.quote: Let $(\bmu,\btheta, Q)\in \PCSB$ such that $\gamma>0$, $\mu_1\geq \epsilon$, and $T>W_T{\log_2 (\ceil{1 + {1}/{\gamma}})}$. Set $\delta=1/T$ in CSB-DT. Then the expected regret of CSB-DT is upper bound as ... for any $\eta$ such that $\forall \ba \in \A, \nabla_{\ba} > 2(k^\star{}^2+2)\eta$ and a problem independent constant $\alpha_1$.

results.notes: Regret-minimisation phase uses CTS (Wang & Chen 2018) with a knapsack oracle, which is NP-hard in general (pseudo-polynomial DP), so compute is marked not_stated. In the paper's appendix the term (K-Q)^2 appears as (K-N)^2. The paper also remarks informally that the regret is O(K log T/nabla_min); this is not recorded.
